questions.problem: Given that $f(x,y)=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{y}),$ find the set of values $(x,y)$ on which $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ exists.
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that $f(x,y)$ is not defined when $y=0.$ So, the domain of $f$ is 

$$
{D}_{f}=\{(x,y)\,:\,y\ne 0\}.
$$

Now, we compute the partial derivatives of $f(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{y})) \\  & =\frac{-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}}{1+{(\frac{x}{y})}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

The function ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ is not defined at the point $(0,0).$ So, the domain of ${f}_{y}$ is

$$
{D}_{{f}_{y}}=\{(x,y)\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\ne 0\}.
$$

Finally, we conclude that the partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $y$ exists on the set

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{f}\cap {D}_{{f}_{y}} & =\{(x,y)\,:\,y\ne 0\}\cap \{(x,y)\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\ne 0\} \\  & =\{(x,y)\,:\,y\ne 0\}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given that $f(x,y,z)=\sqrt{xy-z},$ find the set of values $(x,y,z)$ on which $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ exists.
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that $f(x,y,z)$ is defined only when 

$$
\begin{aligned}xy-z & \ge 0 \\ xy & \ge z.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the domain of $f$ is 

$$
{D}_{f}=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,xy\ge z\}.
$$

Now, we compute the partial derivative of $f(x,y,z)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{xy-z}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{xy-z}}\cdot x \\  & =\frac{x}{2\sqrt{xy-z}}\end{aligned}
$$

The function ${f}_{y}(x,y,z)$ is defined only for 

$$
\begin{aligned}xy-z & >0 \\ xy & >z.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the domain of ${f}_{y}$ is

$$
{D}_{{f}_{y}}=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,xy>z\}.
$$

Finally, we conclude that the partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $y$ exists on the set

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{f}\cap {D}_{{f}_{y}} & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,xy\ge z\}\cap \{(x,y,z)\,:\,xy>z\} \\  & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,xy>z\}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that $h(x,y)=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(xy)$ and

$$
\frac{∂h}{∂x}=-\frac{y}{\sqrt{1-(xy)^{2}}},\,\frac{∂h}{∂y}=-\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-(xy)^{2}}},
$$

find the set of values $(x,y)$ on which all partial derivatives of $h$ exist.
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that $h(x,y)=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(xy)$ is defined only when $-1\le xy\le 1.$ So, the domain of $h$ is 

$$
{D}_{h}=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1\le xy\le 1\}.
$$

As for the partial derivatives, we have the following.

- The function $\frac{∂h}{∂x}=-\frac{y}{\sqrt{1-(xy)^{2}}}$ is defined only when 

$$
\begin{aligned}1-(xy)^{2} & >0 \\ (xy)^{2} & <1 \\ |xy| & <1,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives $-1<xy<1.$ So, the domain of ${h}_{x}$ is 

$$
{D}_{{h}_{x}}=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1<xy<1\}.
$$

- Similarly, the domains of ${h}_{y}$ is the same:

$$
{D}_{{h}_{y}}=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1<xy<1\}.
$$

Finally, we conclude that the partial derivatives of $h$ exist on the set

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{h}\cap {D}_{{h}_{x}}\cap {D}_{{h}_{y}} & ={D}_{h}\cap {D}_{{h}_{x}} \\  & =\{(x,y)\,:\,-1\le xy\le 1\}\cap \{(x,y)\,:\,-1<xy<1\} \\  & =\{(x,y)\,:\,-1<xy<1\}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given that $f(x,y,z)=\frac{z}{\sqrt{x-y}},$ find the set of values $(x,y,z)$ on which $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ exists.
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that $f(x,y,z)$ is defined only when 

$$
\begin{aligned}x-y & >0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the domain of $f$ is 

$$
{D}_{f}=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,x-y>0\}.
$$

Now, we compute the partial derivative of $f(x,y,z)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{z}{\sqrt{x-y}}) \\  & =\frac{z}{2\sqrt{(x-y)^{3}}}\end{aligned}
$$

The function ${f}_{y}(x,y,z)$ is defined only for 

$$
\begin{aligned}x-y>0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the domain of ${f}_{y}$ is

$$
{D}_{{f}_{y}}=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,x-y>0\}.
$$

Finally, we conclude that the partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $y$ exists on the set

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{f}\cap {D}_{{f}_{y}} & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,x-y>0\}\cap \{(x,y,z)\,:\,x-y>0\} \\  & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,x-y>0\}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given that $f(x,y,z)=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+z)}{y},$ find the set of values $(x,y,z)$ on which $\frac{∂f}{∂z}$ exists.
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that $f(x,y,z)$ is defined only when 

$$
\begin{aligned}x+z & >0\,\text{and}\,y\ne 0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the domain of $f$ is 

$$
{D}_{f}=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,x+z>0\,\,\text{and}\,\,y\ne 0\}.
$$

Now, we compute the partial derivative of $f(x,y,z)$ with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{z}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+z)}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{1}{x+z} \\  & =\frac{1}{y(x+z)}\end{aligned}
$$

The function ${f}_{z}(x,y,z)$ is defined only for 

$$
\begin{aligned}x+z & \ne 0\,\text{and}\,y\ne 0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the domain of ${f}_{z}$ is

$$
{D}_{{f}_{z}}=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,x+z\ne 0\,\,\text{and}\,\,y\ne 0\}.
$$

Finally, we conclude that the partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $z$ exists on the set

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{f}\cap {D}_{{f}_{z}} & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,x+z>0\,\,\text{and}\,\,y\ne 0\}\cap \{(x,y,z)\,:\,x+z\ne 0\,\,\text{and}\,\,y\ne 0\} \\  & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,x+z>0\,\,\text{and}\,\,y\ne 0\}.\end{aligned}
$$
